name: isNumber
summary: Returns the value when every part of it is a number, and raises when one is not.

arguments.name: $value
accepts: a number, with or without a unit
a list of numbers, which comes back with the separator it was given
not a value that is only a number in CSS: var(), calc(1rem + 2px) and an interpolated #{5} are refused

caveats: Until 4.0.0 a value that was not a number only warned, and the function then ended with nothing to return, so the build stopped with Sass's own "Function finished without @return" instead of a message naming the argument. It now raises, which is what `isColor` and `isTime` do.

It was also the one of the three that refused a list: `isColor(red blue)` answers both colours and `isTime(0.2s 0.4s)` both times, while `isNumber(10px 20px)` raised, although `margin: 10px 20px` is a shorthand anybody writes. All three take a list since 4.0.0, and all three refuse an empty one with a message of their own.

A `var()`, a `calc()` Sass cannot reduce, and an interpolated `#{5}`, which arrives as a string, are all refused. That is the contract rather than an oversight, and it is what separates this from `isGutter`: a number that comes back from here can be multiplied, and one of those cannot.
